title: From Hijacked PBX to Stolen Trunk: INJ3CTOR3’s Campaign Evolves
content_md: Executive Summary In May, Cyble Research & Intelligence Labs (CRIL) documented JOMANGY , a PHP webshell generation deployed by INJ3CTOR3 with self-healing persistence channels and a built-in toll-fraud dialer. Back then, the fraud ran through the victim's own PBX, so removing the implant would have stopped it. Artifacts we collected from the operator's C2 staging servers during mid-September 2026 show that this is no longer true: the installer now sends credentials off the box on every run, and a second staging host serves it. INJ3CTOR3's FreePBX implant now uploads the victim's SIP trunk, AMI, database, and mail-relay credentials to the operator, so disinfecting or rebuilding an infected host no longer ends the exposure. Anyone running FreePBX, Issabel, or Elastix who suspects compromise must rotate the secrets in 17 configuration files, and only after the host is clean. The infection and persistence code is nearly unchanged; what the operator rotated are the identifiers that were available to defenders since the last time.
